avignonpalaispapes.name: Palais des Papes
avignonpalaispapes.slogan: A fortress of popes, big enough to move a whole papacy into.
avignonpalaispapes.line: Seven popes in a row ruled from Avignon between 1309 and 1377; their palace is the largest Gothic palace in the world.

avignonpontbenezet.name: Pont Saint-Bénezet
avignonpontbenezet.slogan: The bridge that stops halfway, and the song that never does.
avignonpontbenezet.line: The stone bridge once ran 900 metres on 22 arches, yet was only 4.9 metres wide; four arches survive.

orangetheatre.name: Roman Theatre of Orange
orangetheatre.slogan: A 37-metre Roman wall that still carries every voice.
orangetheatre.line: Its stage wall, about 37 metres high, is preserved at its full height, and the theatre seats up to 7,300.

senanqueabbey.name: Sénanque Abbey
senanqueabbey.slogan: Pale stone, purple rows, and monks who still bottle the harvest.
senanqueabbey.line: Founded in 1148, the Cistercian abbey is still home to monks who grow lavender and keep bees.

gordesvillage.name: Gordes
gordesvillage.slogan: A cliffside village stacked like honey-coloured steps.
gordesvillage.line: After the war, Gordes drew artists including Marc Chagall and Victor Vasarely.
